documents.instruction: Keep the three-part mental model exact: Skarbiec credential boundary, bounded IMAP-to-SQLite synchronization, and idempotency-keyed SMTP replies.
Clone-to-first-mailbox path with only output captured from the isolated 0.2.0 CLI and HTTP run; never fabricate provider success.
Complete command, option, default, output, namespace, and exit-code reference for the Clap surface.
Every loopback route, authentication rule, body, bound, and response semantic must match the v1 router and public models.
List every CLI knob, environment reader, mailbox key, Skarbiec field, fixed item ID, default, and compiled safety bound; never include a credential value.
State what Skrzynka owns and does not own, data flow, durable state, concurrency, and every trust boundary from source.
Symptom-first operations guide covering every stable public error family and exact source sentence, with safe recovery and no secrets.
Preserve the real isolated 0.2.0 CLI transcript for status, add, duplicate refusal, sync failure, state transitions, and confirmed removal.
Preserve the real isolated HTTP transcript proving loopback readiness, fail-closed authentication, identity failure, and generic callback errors.
Mailbox shape, precedence, lifecycle, organization ownership, validation, and exact refusals.
Message normalization shape, mailbox-UID identity, lifecycle, bounds, immutable behavior, and refusals.
Reply attempt state machine, idempotency, SMTP acceptance boundary, recovery, message construction, and exact refusals.
One-pass algorithm, scheduling, cursor semantics, all-vs-one output, limits, and actual lack of configured IMAP network timeout.
Canonical item shapes, child-process protocol, secret lifetime, bounds, lifecycle, and exact refusal families.

OAuth and Workspace-delegation lifecycles, fixed items, endpoint trust, token lifetime, invariants, and refusal families.

Core resource and failure contract with exact limits; never claim an IMAP timeout unless the client path configures one.
Skarbiec, IMAP, SMTP, Google, identity, desktop, and onboarding boundaries; capabilities and reliability must match source.
Zero state, first-success evidence, machine and desktop journeys, common failures, and destructive reset boundary.
Version authority, development channel, schema/API compatibility, stopped-service upgrade, rollback, and uncertain-send recovery.
Index every runnable example, its side-effect risk, prerequisites, evidence boundary, cleanup, and next step.
Runnable isolated-state CLI sequence for add, bounded sync, and observation; never accept or print credentials.
Provider-facing reply example must require explicit confirmation, inspect the target first, and use one fresh idempotency key.
Destructive local-only removal example must require confirmation, inspect before deletion, and state the recovery boundary.
Authenticated loopback-only HTTP sequence with protected temporary headers, exact route bodies, and no credential field.
